# Copilot instructions for js-genai

Goal: Help AI coding agents contribute productively to this TypeScript SDK (@google/genai) with minimal ramp-up.

## Big picture
- Library exposes a single public entry: `GoogleGenAI` plus submodules. Public surface is re-exported from `src/index.ts`; Node/Web specific builds are in `src/node` and `src/web` and selected via package exports in `package.json`.
- Core runtime pieces:
  - `src/client.ts` / `src/node/node_client.ts` / `src/web/web_client.ts`: construct the top-level client, wire auth, transports, and submodules.
  - `src/_api_client.ts`: HTTP core (base URL/version, headers, streaming, error handling). Do not break its request contract; all modules depend on it.
  - Submodules expose API groups: `models`, `live`, `chats`, `files`, `caches`, `batches`, `operations`, `tokens`, `tunings`, `fileSearchStores`.
  - Transports: upload/download and websockets are environment-specific (`src/node/_node_*`, `src/cross/_cross_*`).
  - Type conversion: `src/_transformers.ts` and `src/converters/**` map SDK-friendly inputs to API JSON and back.
- Many files are generated: look for “Code generated by the Google Gen AI SDK generator DO NOT EDIT.” Examples: `src/models.ts`, `src/types.ts`. Prefer changes in helpers/transformers instead of editing generated files.

## Environment, auth, and base URLs
- Node client resolves options from both constructor and env with precedence rules (see `src/node/node_client.ts`):
  - You may not pass both `project/location` and `apiKey` together (throws).
  - When `vertexai: true`, explicit `googleAuthOptions.credentials` takes precedence over API key; `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`/`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` take precedence over env API key when both present; defaults `location` to `global` if needed.
- Base URL/version logic:
  - Defaults live in `src/_api_client.ts` (v1beta for Gemini, v1beta1 for Vertex).
  - Override via `HttpOptions.baseUrl`, or via `setDefaultBaseUrls` in `src/_base_url.ts`, or env in Node (`GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`).
- User-Agent and SDK version are set in `_api_client.ts` (`SDK_VERSION` tagged by release-please). Don’t edit manually.

## Key coding patterns to follow
- Content normalization: Always pass user input through `tContents(...)` from `src/_transformers.ts` when building requests (see `models.generateContent` for example usage and AFC loop).
- Streaming: Use `ApiClient.streamRequest*` and `responseLineRE` handling already implemented in `_api_client.ts` rather than re-implementing SSE parsing.
- Automatic Function Calling (AFC): `src/_afc.ts` implements tool orchestration; modules call `hasCallableTools` and `shouldDisableAfc` and maintain `automaticFunctionCallingHistory`. Keep this flow intact when adding features that touch tools.
- Errors: Throw `ApiError` (`src/errors.ts`) for HTTP failures; do not throw raw fetch errors.
- Pagers: For list APIs use `Pager` from `src/pagers.ts` and implement `PagedItem` mapping.

## Build, lint, test, docs
- Node >= 20 is required. Typical dev loop:
  - Build: `npm run build` (rollup + api-extractor; runs patches and ignores optional MCP dep in dev).
  - Unit tests: `npm run unit-test` (tsc to `dist/` then jasmine on `dist/test/unit/**/*_test.js`).
  - System tests (require env/project): `npm run test-server-tests` (CI sets sample `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`/`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`).
  - Lint/format: `npm run lint` and `npm run format`.
  - Docs: `npm run docs` generates TypeDoc and adds license headers. CI pushes docs via `.github/workflows/pages.yml` using `scripts/generate_pages.ts`.
  - API surface consistency: `scripts/validate_api_consistency.sh` checks `api-report/*` parity across cross/node/web—run it if you touch exports.

## Public surface and exports
- Public API is gathered via `src/index.ts` and environment entries `src/node/index.ts`, `src/web/index.ts`; rollup bundles according to `rollup.config.mjs` and `package.json` `exports`. If you add a new public symbol, export it from these entry points and keep node/web parity.
- Any new public type or method must be reflected in API reports (`api-extractor.*.json`), and CI will fail if cross/node/web APIs diverge.

## Examples in-repo
- Usage samples live in `sdk-samples/` and `google_samples/`; tests under `test/unit` and `test/system` show supported patterns (e.g., streaming, files, chats, MCP via `mcpToTool`). Prefer aligning new features with these examples.

## Avoid
- Editing generated files (`src/models.ts`, `src/types.ts`, converters generated files) unless updating the generator. Prefer helpers/transformers.
- Introducing Node-only or Web-only APIs in shared modules. Mirror changes across `src/node` and `src/web` and keep `api-report` consistent.

If anything above is unclear (e.g., AFC flow, base URL precedence, or where to surface a new API), tell me which change you want to make; I’ll point to the exact files and patterns to follow.
